passages.t: ‘Give me an undivided heart’: a prayer of David in Book Three
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “A prayer of David” (verse 1). It is the only psalm in Book Three whose heading names David. It begins, “Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy” (verse 1).

The prayer piles up requests: preserve me, be merciful, bring joy, hear me (verses 2 to 6). Then it turns to praise. “O Lord, there is none like You among the gods, nor any works like Yours” (verse 8). “All the nations You have made will come and bow before You” (verse 9). “For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God” (verse 10).

In the middle is one of the best prayers in the Psalms. “Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name” (verse 11).

Danger is real: “a band of ruthless men seeks my life” (verse 14). And then the psalm quotes God's own words about himself: “But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness” (verse 15).
passages.hearers:
Verse 15 is almost word for word what God said to Moses on Mount Sinai. There, after the people had made a golden calf, God passed by Moses and called out his own name: “The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness” (Exodus 34:6). These words come back again and again in the Old Testament. Here a man in danger holds them up to God and says: this is who you said you are.

Much of this psalm is made of lines found elsewhere in Scripture. That is not a weakness. It is how people who know Scripture pray. They pray it back.

‘The son of Your maidservant’ (verse 16) was a phrase for a servant born in a household. He belonged to that house from birth. To say it to God is to say: I have always been yours.

‘I am godly’ (verse 2) is not a boast of being perfect. The Hebrew word means loyal, one who belongs to God and has not left him. The book page's part on claims of innocence says more.
passages.later:
Moses heard the words of verse 15 first (Exodus 34:6). Jonah complained that God was exactly this kind of God, because God spared Nineveh (Jonah 4:2).

Verse 9 is picked up in Revelation: “All nations will come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been revealed” (Revelation 15:4).
passages.asks:
Pray verse 11 slowly. ‘Give me an undivided heart.’ Most of us are pulled many ways at once. This prayer asks God to gather the pieces into one heart that fears him.

And when you are in trouble, try praying God's own words back to him, as this psalm does. Read Exodus 34:6 aloud and say, ‘Lord, this is who you are. Be this to me.’
